text:
incident-bot: ALERT — streaming latency breach detected for /v1/stream (us-west-2a)
- metric: preproc.expand_template.p99 = 2500ms (SLO 1500ms)
- symptom: streaming stalls and increased tail latency observed
- sample_trace: trace=tr_9c8b2f

maya: taking this. paging eng-oncall and eng-runtime. @here

liam (eng-oncall): on the page, grabbing traces and topo. paste the hot spans pls.

maya: attaching the top spans and a quick grep from preproc logs:
```
span preproc.expand_template duration=1700ms
span preproc.serialize_tool_schema duration=900ms
span streaming.emit duration=120ms
logs: preproc INFO "expanded_tokens=19840" template=tpl/complex_order_v3
logs: preproc WARN "schema_serialize=935ms" req=xyz789
```

maya: looks like the expansion step plus schema serialization are dominating p99. pushed template changes last night (PR #4937).

dave (eng-runtime): that PR added deep expansion of tool inputs when json_mode=true. it explodes for nested tool graphs — saw it in canary perf but masked by low traffic.

priya (eng-ml): is this limited to specific routes/customers or model variants?

maya: observed on /v1/stream and /v1/completions when customers use structured templates (json_mode=true) with nested tool schemas. affects hosted + dedicated nodes in us-west-2a. baseline p95 ~620ms -> now ~1100ms, p99 ~1.5s -> 2.5s.

jess (support): flagged three accounts seeing streaming stalls. creating PS tickets and notifying CS. Tickets: CS-8201, CS-8204, CS-8210.

aaron (customer-success): i'll prepare a short customer-facing update. need impact summary and mitigations.

maya: immediate mitigations to consider (ordered by risk):
1) flip feature flag to use shallow_expand mode for templates (disables deep recursive expansion)
2) scale preproc worker replicas: kubectl scale deploy/preproc --replicas=12
3) route streaming traffic to dedicated low-latency pool via routing rules
4) revert PR #4937 if rollback safe

liam: i'll shadow the flag flip. which service owns FF?

deploy-bot: feature-flag endpoint available. example patch:
```
curl -X POST "https://flags.redwood/api/v1/flags" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN" -d '{"template_expand_mode":"shallow"}'
```

maya: applying shallow mode now. will watch metric and traces.

~1.5 minutes later~

maya: update: after switching to shallow expand, p99 dropped from 2500ms -> 980ms. p95 returned ~650ms. streaming stall rate down significantly. immediate improvement confirmed.

priya: that delta implies our expansion was worse than linear for nested inputs. we should add a max_depth and protect against pathological templates.

dave: opening hotfix branch fix/limit-template-expand to cap depth and add a fast-path cache for serialized schemas per template+model hash. will run a quick canary.

maya: we also scaled preproc to 12 which helped drain backlog; will downscale once steady.

liam: taking over on-call. maya, please post a concise handoff message and include current state and next steps.

maya: handoff summary: cause = deep recursive template expansion (PR #4937) + heavy schema serialization path. immediate mitigation = feature_flag(template_expand_mode=shallow) + scaled preproc workers. customer impact = streaming stalls for 3 customers in us-west-2a, p99 peaked at 2.5s, now ~980ms. owners: priya (RCA), dave (runtime fix), jess/aaron (customer comms).

liam: creating incident INC-2029-0702 and will coordinate postmortem. I will keep this channel updated every 60m or on new findings.

aaron: sending customer note now. next customer update ETA 90m. note will include workaround: avoid nested tool calls or set json_mode=false temporarily.

jess: added quick-run support doc for CS explaining the rollback/flag toggle and suggested customer messaging.

priya: starting a reproducibility job to vary nesting depth and measure p99. preliminary hypothesis: capping depth=3 should keep p99 < 1s. ETA for initial numbers: 3h.

dave: pushed draft PR fix/limit-template-expand; will run canary in eu-west-1 in ~45m.

liam: action items logged:
- priya: reproducer + perf figures (ETA 3h)
- dave: PR + canary + cache (ETA 2h)
- maya: monitor metrics and scale down preproc when stable
- aaron/jess: customer comms + ticket updates
- liam (oncall): incident owner until RCA posted

maya: i'm going off-call. ping me if rollback required. good work.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: partially mitigated. p99 below SLO after mitigation. Incident owner: liam. Ticket: INC-2029-0702.
